research_mode: official MHCLG accredited statistical bulletin only; fail-closed limitations; no parcel score, candidate value or business result

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Lift release incidents
verified_claims: Lift release was the largest category in the remaining non-fire group, with 13,760 incidents.
limitations: Lift-release volume is service-demand evidence, not a general public-safety score.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Dwelling fire fatalities
verified_claims: There were 184 fire-related fatalities in dwelling fires, 72% of all fire-related fatalities and 14% fewer than the previous year.
limitations: National dwelling-fatality figures cannot be assigned to an individual dwelling.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Fatal primary-fire ratio
verified_claims: The 239 fires with at least one fatality represented 0.36% of primary fires.
limitations: A national ratio is not an actuarial probability for a specific building and is sensitive to small counts.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Primary-fire response time
verified_claims: The average total response time to primary fires was 9 minutes 25 seconds, 19 seconds longer than the previous year.
limitations: National average response time hides local station, geography, traffic and incident-type variation.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Secondary-fire response time
verified_claims: The average total response time to secondary fires was 9 minutes 58 seconds, 36 seconds longer than the previous year.
limitations: Secondary-fire response times may fluctuate with incident volumes and do not predict response to a parcel.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Incident data platform transition
verified_claims: Incident data were collected through the Incident Recording System until November 2025 and through the Fire and Rescue Data Platform from then onward.
limitations: A system transition can affect data continuity and requires caution in time-series interpretation.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Data snapshot and revisions
verified_claims: The published figures use incidents up to the end of March 2026 submitted by 12 May 2026, and later revisions may occur.
limitations: The release is a database snapshot and may differ from later local records, especially for small counts.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Suffolk data limitation
verified_claims: Suffolk Fire and Rescue Service could not submit all incidents between September 2024 and June 2025, so figures for that period are underestimated.
limitations: Affected Suffolk comparisons must be treated as incomplete and cannot support high-confidence local scoring.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Accredited official statistics status
verified_claims: The release is identified as accredited official statistics under the Code of Practice for Statistics.
limitations: Accreditation supports production quality but does not make national aggregates parcel-level evidence.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Primary-fire definition
verified_claims: Primary fires include incidents in non-derelict buildings, vehicles or outdoor structures, incidents involving a fatality, casualty or rescue, or incidents attended by five or more pumping appliances.
limitations: The classification is operational and does not by itself quantify severity or risk for any particular property.
